subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (The Four Kinds Of State, The Colocation Rule, The Server-State Distinction, URL State Decision Rule, Anti-Patterns And Their Fixes, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current frontend practice (Kent C. Dodds colocation, React Query/SWR server-state model, URL-as-state, single source of truth).

cases.scenario: A team holds all fetched API data (users, orders, products) in a single Redux store, and has written custom middleware for refetch-on-focus, request deduplication, cache expiry, and post-mutation invalidation. Each piece has subtle bugs.
cases.context: React SPA. The team is debugging stale-data and double-fetch issues.
cases.question: How should the agent reclassify and restructure this state?
expected_flags: The fetched API data is server state, which a general-purpose store does not handle by default
Server state has four properties (remote canonical source, dedup, staleness, mutation-triggered invalidation) the custom middleware is badly reimplementing
Migrate server data to a server-state library (React Query / SWR / RTK Query / Apollo); keep the general store for genuinely client UI state only
The custom refetch/dedup/expiry/invalidation middleware is reinventing React Query, badly
expected_fix_hints: Move users/orders/products into useQuery hooks keyed by query key
Use mutate-then-invalidate-by-key instead of manual cache expiry middleware
absent_signals: Do not keep server data in the general-purpose store

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: The fetched API data is server state, which a general-purpose store does not handle by default.
Surfaces this expected flag: Server state has four properties (remote canonical source, dedup, staleness, mutation-triggered invalidation) the custom middleware is badly reimplementing.
Surfaces this expected flag: Migrate server data to a server-state library (React Query / SWR / RTK Query / Apollo); keep the general store for genuinely client UI state only.
Surfaces this expected flag: The custom refetch/dedup/expiry/invalidation middleware is reinventing React Query, badly.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Move users/orders/products into useQuery hooks keyed by query key.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Use mutate-then-invalidate-by-key instead of manual cache expiry middleware.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep server data in the general-purpose store.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep hand-building refetch/dedup/invalidation.

cases.scenario: A product listing keeps the active category filter, sort order, and page number in component useState. Users report that the back-button doesn't restore their view, refreshing loses their filters, and they can't share a link to a filtered view.
cases.context: Next.js App Router page with a responsive listing grid.
cases.question: Where should this state live and why?
expected_flags: Filter, sort, and page are URL-worthy: 'should two people opening this URL see the same view?' is yes
Move them to URL state (useSearchParams / route params), not component state
URL state fixes the back-button, survives refresh, and makes the view shareable
Consider a type-safe URL-state library (nuqs) for serialization/parsing
expected_fix_hints: Adopt nuqs for type-safe URL state
absent_signals: Do not keep filter/sort/page in component useState
Do not put this in a global store either — the URL is the owner

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Filter, sort, and page are URL-worthy: 'should two people opening this URL see the same view?' is yes.
Surfaces this expected flag: Move them to URL state (useSearchParams / route params), not component state.
Surfaces this expected flag: URL state fixes the back-button, survives refresh, and makes the view shareable.
Surfaces this expected flag: Consider a type-safe URL-state library (nuqs) for serialization/parsing.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Read/write filter+sort+page via useSearchParams.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Adopt nuqs for type-safe URL state.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep filter/sort/page in component useState.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not put this in a global store either — the URL is the owner.

cases.scenario: A new feature needs a small toggle state used by exactly one component. A developer adds it to the app-wide Zustand store 'to be consistent with how we do state here.' The store has grown to 80 keys, many unread for months.
cases.context: React app where global-store-by-default is the established (but unexamined) habit.
cases.question: How should the agent advise placing this state?
expected_flags: Start local: a toggle used by one component belongs in that component's useState, not the global store
Premature globalization causes state sprawl — the store grows and nobody knows what's in it
Only lift on observed need (a second consumer); only reach for a store when many components depend on many slices of a frequently-changing value
Recommend auditing the store for entries unread in N months
expected_fix_hints: Use local useState for the single-component toggle
Lift only when a second consumer genuinely appears
absent_signals: Do not add single-component state to the global store
Do not justify placement by 'consistency with existing habit'

cases.scenario: The selected item id is stored both in a parent component's useState and copied into a child's local useState on mount. Updates in the parent don't reflect in the child, producing 'I changed it but it still shows the old value' bugs.
cases.context: React component tree with a parent list and a child detail panel.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the state ownership?
expected_flags: This is duplicated state — the same value held in two independent locations, violating single source of truth
Identify the canonical owner (the parent) and have the child read from it (props/context) rather than copying
Derive in the other location or sync explicitly with a recorded reason if a copy is truly needed
Updates fail to propagate precisely because there are two sources of truth
expected_fix_hints: Pass selectedId down as a prop; remove the child's copied useState
If a copy is unavoidable, add an explicit sync mechanism and document why
absent_signals: Do not keep two independent copies of the same value
Do not 'fix' it by adding more sync code without naming the canonical owner

cases.scenario: A cart component stores the cart items AND a separate stored `totalPrice` field that it manually keeps in sync; it also applies optimistic updates to a 'redeem promo code' mutation that frequently fails server-side validation, leaving users confused.
cases.question: How should the agent review the derived-state and optimistic-update choices?
expected_flags: totalPrice is derived state that is being stored — compute it at read time instead, so it can't go stale
Only store derived values with measured performance evidence (and then memoize, e.g. useMemo)
Optimistic updates are for high-confidence mutations only; the frequently-failing promo redemption should be pessimistic (loading → success/error)
Where optimistic updates are used, a rollback path must exist
expected_fix_hints: Replace stored totalPrice with a read-time computation
Switch the low-confidence promo mutation to pessimistic UI
absent_signals: Do not keep a manually-synced stored total
Do not apply optimistic UI to a high-failure mutation

cases.scenario: A teammate asks the state-management owner to (a) pick between Redux Toolkit and Zustand for the project, and (b) design the JSON response shape for the new /orders API endpoint.
cases.context: The team treats 'state' as covering both library choice and API design.
cases.question: How should the agent scope these requests?
expected_flags: Choosing between Redux Toolkit and Zustand is a tactical, library-specific decision below this skill — defer to library docs + framework conventions
Designing the JSON shape of the /orders endpoint is api-design's territory (the external request/response surface)
This skill owns where the response data lives once it arrives and how it is invalidated, not the endpoint shape or the store library
Correctly redirects rather than answering the library-choice or API-shape question out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Route the library choice to library docs / team conventions
Route the API response shape to api-design
absent_signals: Do not pick the state library here
Do not design the API response shape here

cases.scenario: A team puts all user preferences (including a 'compact mode' that must be reflected in the first server-rendered paint, and cross-device) into localStorage. On first SSR render the server doesn't know the preference, causing a flash and no cross-device sync.
cases.context: Next.js App Router app with SSR and authenticated users.
cases.question: How should the agent reclassify these preferences?
expected_flags: Preferences that affect SSR or must sync across devices are not local-only — localStorage is the wrong owner
Server-side store (or cookie the server can read) for prefs that affect SSR, so the first paint is correct
URL state for session-scoped prefs; localStorage only when local-only is genuinely correct
Match the persistent-state choice to what the data actually needs (localStorage / IndexedDB / cookies / server-stored)
expected_fix_hints: Move SSR-affecting + cross-device prefs to a server-stored profile (or readable cookie)
Keep only genuinely local-only prefs in localStorage
absent_signals: Do not keep SSR-affecting preferences in localStorage only
Do not assume localStorage gives cross-device sync
